# ASTRA Scientific Closure: Forward-only port completion of an adjoint

Date: 15 October 2026 (Australia/Brisbane)

## Scientific status

This investigation produced an exact conditional linear-algebra construction, synthetic tests, and a reanalysis of published objective traces. It did NOT establish a fundamentally new scientific operation, integrated physical validation of the construction, superiority to the strongest available methods, or an exceptionally consequential technological advance. Historical novelty is unknown; the mathematics combines established adjoint sensitivity, Schur complements, and low-rank inverse updates. No independent review has occurred.

The candidate operation is useful only when all nonreciprocity is confined to a small, physically known set of accessible ports. The experiment does not certify that assumption. Unknown reciprocal background components are allowed. Unknown control derivatives are not supplied for free.

## Decision

At a fixed operating point, choose local settings of a physical linear network to improve a measurable objective. This is a local control decision, not a guarantee of global optimization or finite-step improvement. The interest is acquiring many sensitivities without reconstructing every hidden component or physically building the transpose network.

Strong alternatives must be tried first: randomized comparisons of available settings; two-sided random-direction estimators; multiplexed perturbations; direct forward tangent-source measurements for a few candidate directions; ordinary reciprocal physical adjoints; and applicable same-hardware transformations for nonreciprocal systems. A cheaper exact full gradient need not outperform an inexpensive approximate direction on the actual decision.

Conversely strict positivity of sym K implies K invertible and sym(K^{-1}) positive. All claims below are within this open static accretive cone, without a supplied uniform norm or coercivity bound.

Let the nonzero objective source c belong to V, as in the incoming closure protocol. For any target tangent source q outside V, the scalar c^T K q can assume every real value while all those responses remain exactly unchanged.

Choose an orthonormal basis for V and its complement, and write

    K = [[H,Z],[G,T]].

The measured columns fix H and G. S=sym H is strictly positive. Choose any Z and set

    C=(Z+G^T)/2,

# Task-restricted completion and validation of a physical adjoint

Date 2026-10-15. Internal mathematical derivations and synthetic checks.
Source pin `b7cada92d2eb304578be5ed974f1e44b10a89928`. No laboratory evidence,
historical novelty or independent mathematical review is asserted.

The proposed operation is a physical use of established dot-product testing
and independent Gaussian residual validation. It can acquire task-specific
accuracy without acquiring a global nonreciprocity support certificate.
It does require additional injection access on the relevant control-force
space, and its amplitude/precision costs cannot be hidden in a profile count.

## 1. Incoming construction reconstructed

At one fixed loaded real linear operating point, write Ax=b, J=F(x,p),
c=F_x and lambda=A^{-T}c. A parameter direction d has tangent force
f_d=b'_d-A'_d x and first derivative F'_d+f_d^T lambda.

Under the supplied port hypothesis A=R+PKP^T with R symmetric, acquire
Y=A^{-1}P, z=A^{-1}c, H=P^T Y. For invertible A and H, the incoming estimate is

\[
 \alpha=H^{-1}P^Tz,\quad
 \beta=H^{-1}(H^T-H)\alpha,\quad
 \hat\lambda=z+Y\beta.                                    \tag{1}
\]

Put D0=K^T-K. Then A^T=A+P D0 P^T and the low-rank inverse identity gives
H^T=(I+H D0)^{-1}H. Inverting this identity shows
D=H^{-T}-H^{-1}=D0. Thus A^T=A+PDP^T, and (1) solves the adjoint.
The acquisition uses b, k port profiles and c, with the same A and calibrated
source/sensor loading. Only rows needed for port solves and control forces
need be stored. The interior need not be reconstructed, but the port support
premise is not supplied by this acquisition.

The exact source pair A±=I±e2 e4^T, b=e1, c=e2, P=[e3,e5], v=e1-e4 has
identical full responses to all protocol profiles. Its conductance update

minimum eigenvalue 1/2. This falsifies support certification, not (1) under
its actual hypothesis. The source empirical trace reanalysis concerns an
established reciprocal baseline, not an experiment on (1).
